Panchala.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Panchala.question: Shaunakayaniputra _____, ruler of Ahichatra, whom Vaidehiputra Ashadhasena mentioned as his grandfather in his Pabhosa inscription, is identified with king Vangapala, known from his coins
Panchala.fact: The names of the rulers found on these coins are Vangapala, Yajnapala, Damagupta, Rudragupta, Jayagupta, Suryamitra, Phalgunimitra, Bhanumitra, Bhumimitra, Dhruvamitra, Agnimitra, Indramitra, Vishnumitra, Jayamitra, Prajapatimitra, Varunamitra, Anamitra, Bhadraghosha and Yugasena (the reverse of the coins of Varunamitra, Yugasena and Anamitra do not exhibit any deity). Panchala.question: The name of _____ is also found on a clay sealing
Panchala.fact: The names of the rulers found on these coins are Vangapala, Yajnapala, Damagupta, Rudragupta, Jayagupta, Suryamitra, Phalgunimitra, Bhanumitra, Bhumimitra, Dhruvamitra, Agnimitra, Indramitra, Vishnumitra, Jayamitra, Prajapatimitra, Varunamitra, Anamitra, Bhadraghosha and Yugasena (the reverse of the coins of Varunamitra, Yugasena and Anamitra do not exhibit any deity). Panchala.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Panchala.question: The coins of _____ found from Ahichatra have a wheel of eight spokes on the reverse and the legend Achyu on the obverse
Panchala.fact: The last independent ruler of Ahichatra was Achyuta, who was defeated by Samudragupta, after which Panchala was annexed into the Gupta Empire. The coins of Achyuta found from Ahichatra have a wheel of eight spokes on the reverse and the legend Achyu on the obverse.

Panchala.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Panchala.question: 1100–500 BCE), it was one of the most powerful states of ancient India, closely allied with the _____ kingdom
Panchala.fact: 1100–500 BCE), it was one of the most powerful states of ancient India, closely allied with the Kuru kingdom. Its western neighbours were the Sūrasenas and the Yakṛllomas, while in the north-west it was separated from the Ganga and the Kurus by dense forests.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: The _____ was Group of five brothers in the epic Mahabharata.
Pandava.fact: The Pandavas (Sanskrit: पाण्डव, IAST: Pāṇḍava) is a patronymic referring to the five legendary brothers, Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva, who are central figures of the ancient Hindu epic Mahabharata. In the epic, the Pandavas married Draupadi, the princess of Panchala, and set up the city of Indraprastha after the Kuru Kingdom was split to avoid succession disputes.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: They are acknowledged as the sons of _____, the King of Kuru, but were fathered by different Devas (gods) due to Pandu's cursed inability to naturally sire children
Pandava.fact: They are acknowledged as the sons of Pandu, the King of Kuru, but were fathered by different Devas (gods) due to Pandu's cursed inability to naturally sire children.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: After the split, the other part of the kingdom was ruled by their cousins, the _____
Pandava.fact: After the split, the other part of the kingdom was ruled by their cousins, the Kauravas. However, the Pandavas lost their kingdom to Duryodhana (eldest and king of the Kauravas) when Yudhishthira gambled it away during a game of dice.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: After this time the _____ refused to return the kingdom
Pandava.fact: After the split, the other part of the kingdom was ruled by their cousins, the Kauravas. However, the Pandavas lost their kingdom to Duryodhana (eldest and king of the Kauravas) when Yudhishthira gambled it away during a game of dice.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Bhima is described being fair-golden complexioned (_____), plump, long-armed and tall as a full-grown Sala tree
Pandava.fact: Bhima is described being fair-golden complexioned (Gaura), plump, long-armed and tall as a full-grown Sala tree.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He was the one dearest to Kunti, and intent on doing what is agreeable to _____
Pandava.fact: He was the one dearest to Kunti, and intent on doing what is agreeable to Yudhishthira.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He is also praised to be always mindful of the duties of _____ (warrior -class), and would sacrifice his own life than say anything that is opposed to morals
Pandava.fact: He is also praised to be always mindful of the duties of Kshatriyas (warrior -class), and would sacrifice his own life than say anything that is opposed to morals.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He married Kunti, a princess of the Yadu clan, and Madri, the princess of _____
Pandava.fact: He married Kunti, a princess of the Yadu clan, and Madri, the princess of Madra Kingdom.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: However, they turn out to be a sage named _____ and his wife, who had used their divine powers to take the form of the animals
Pandava.fact: However, they turn out to be a sage named Kindama and his wife, who had used their divine powers to take the form of the animals. Enraged, Kindama berated the king for having killed him before he had finished the act of mating and before dying, he cursed Pandu that he would die the moment he touched his wife intending to have sex.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Enraged, _____ berated the king for having killed him before he had finished the act of mating and before dying, he cursed Pandu that he would die the moment he touched his wife intending to have sex
Pandava.fact: However, they turn out to be a sage named Kindama and his wife, who had used their divine powers to take the form of the animals. Enraged, Kindama berated the king for having killed him before he had finished the act of mating and before dying, he cursed Pandu that he would die the moment he touched his wife intending to have sex.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: After the event Pandu voluntarily renounced royal life as penance, leaving the _____ under Dhritarashtra
Pandava.fact: After the event Pandu voluntarily renounced royal life as penance, leaving the Kingdom under Dhritarashtra.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Kunti and _____ accompanied Pandu and together they lived in a forest
Pandava.fact: Kunti and Madri accompanied Pandu and together they lived in a forest. The first three of the Pandavas were the sons of Kunti, while the younger two were born to Madri after Kunti shared her mantra with her at Pandu's request.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Before her marriage, Kunti was blessed with a boon by the sage _____, that she could have a son by any god whom she respects without having any marital affair
Pandava.fact: Before her marriage, Kunti was blessed with a boon by the sage Durvasa, that she could have a son by any god whom she respects without having any marital affair.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: This plotting took a grave turn when _____ had to relent to the will of the masses and rightfully appointed his nephew Yudhishthira as crown prince
Pandava.fact: This plotting took a grave turn when Dhritarashtra had to relent to the will of the masses and rightfully appointed his nephew Yudhishthira as crown prince. This went against the personal ambitions of both father and son (Dhritarashtra and Duryodhana) and drove Duryodhana into such a rage that he enthusiastically agreed to an evil ploy by Shakuni to murder Yudhishthira.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Shakuni commissioned the construction of a palace in _____, secretly built by incorporating flammable materials like oil, ghee etc
Pandava.fact: Shakuni commissioned the construction of a palace in Varnavarta, secretly built by incorporating flammable materials like oil, ghee etc. Duryodhana then successfully lobbied Dhritarashtra to send Yudhishthira to represent the royal household in Varnavarta during the celebrations of Shiva Mahotsava.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: This palace was known as _____
Pandava.fact: This palace was called Lakshagriha.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Duryodhana then successfully lobbied _____ to send Yudhishthira to represent the royal household in Varnavarta during the celebrations of Shiva Mahotsava
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana then successfully lobbied Dhritarashtra to send Yudhishthira to represent the royal household in Varnavarta during the celebrations of Shiva Mahotsava.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: The plan was to set the palace on fire during the night while _____ would likely be asleep
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana then successfully lobbied Dhritarashtra to send Yudhishthira to represent the royal household in Varnavarta during the celebrations of Shiva Mahotsava. The plan was to set the palace on fire during the night while Yudhishthira would likely be asleep.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Yudhishthira left for _____, accompanied by his four brothers and their mother Kunti
Pandava.fact: Yudhishthira left for Varnavrata, accompanied by his four brothers and their mother Kunti.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: The plan was discovered by their paternal uncle _____, who was very loyal to them and an extraordinarily wise man
Pandava.fact: The plan was discovered by their paternal uncle Vidura, who was very loyal to them and an extraordinarily wise man. Vidura arranged for a tunnel to be secretly built for the Pandavas to safely escape the palace as it was set afire.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: In addition, _____ had been forewarned about this plot by a hermit who came to him and spoke of an imminent disaster
Pandava.fact: The plan was to set the palace on fire during the night while Yudhishthira would likely be asleep. Yudhishthira left for Varnavrata, accompanied by his four brothers and their mother Kunti.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: The Adi Parva narrates that after their flight from the palace, the five brothers lived in the forests for some time disguised as _____
Pandava.fact: The Adi Parva narrates that after their flight from the palace, the five brothers lived in the forests for some time disguised as Brahmins.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: They heard from a group of travelling sages about a contest (svayamvara) being held in the _____ of Panchala that offered Draupadi's hand in marriage to the winner
Pandava.fact: They heard from a group of travelling sages about a contest (svayamvara) being held in the Kingdom of Panchala that offered Draupadi's hand in marriage to the winner.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: The svayamvara turned out to rely on the skills of archery, and _____, who was a peerless archer, entered the competition and won
Pandava.fact: The svayamvara turned out to rely on the skills of archery, and Arjuna, who was a peerless archer, entered the competition and won.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: When the brothers took _____ to introduce her to their mother, they jokingly announced to Kunti that they had arrived with excellent alms
Pandava.fact: They heard from a group of travelling sages about a contest (svayamvara) being held in the Kingdom of Panchala that offered Draupadi's hand in marriage to the winner. When the brothers took Draupadi to introduce her to their mother, they jokingly announced to Kunti that they had arrived with excellent alms.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Kunti was busy with some work and replied without turning to look at _____ (who the alms referred to) ordering the brothers to share the alms equally amongst the five of them
Pandava.fact: They heard from a group of travelling sages about a contest (svayamvara) being held in the Kingdom of Panchala that offered Draupadi's hand in marriage to the winner. When the brothers took Draupadi to introduce her to their mother, they jokingly announced to Kunti that they had arrived with excellent alms.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Bhima had two other wives—the rakshasi (demoness) _____ and Valandhara, a princess of the Kingdom of Kashi
Pandava.fact: Bhima had two other wives—the rakshasi (demoness) Hidimbi and Valandhara, a princess of the Kingdom of Kashi. Hidimbi was the mother of Ghatotkacha, while Savarga was the son of Valandhara.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Hidimbi was the mother of _____, while Savarga was the son of Valandhara
Pandava.fact: Hidimbi was the mother of Ghatotkacha, while Savarga was the son of Valandhara.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Nakula had a wife named _____, daughter of king of Chedi, and had a son named Niramitra
Pandava.fact: Nakula had a wife named Karenumati, daughter of king of Chedi, and had a son named Niramitra.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Sahadeva was married to _____, princess of Madra, and had a son named Suhotra
Pandava.fact: Sahadeva was married to Vijaya, princess of Madra, and had a son named Suhotra.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Simon Brodbeck theorizes that these marriages might have taken place after the _____, as these unnamed wives not mentioned elsewhere
Pandava.fact: Simon Brodbeck theorizes that these marriages might have taken place after the Kurukshetra War, as these unnamed wives not mentioned elsewhere.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: However, in their absence, _____ had succeeded in being made the crown prince
Pandava.fact: However, in their absence, Duryodhana had succeeded in being made the crown prince. He retained the developed Hastinapura for himself and Duryodhana and gave the barren, arid and hostile lands of Khandavaprastha to the Pandavas.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Owing to this, bet after bet, _____ lost all of his wealth, and eventually his kingdom, in the game
Pandava.fact: Owing to this, bet after bet, Yudhishthira lost all of his wealth, and eventually his kingdom, in the game. Yudhishthira fell for it and put his brothers at stake, losing them too.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He was then enticed by _____ and Shakuni to place his brothers as bets
Pandava.fact: Eventually Shakuni sired yet another plot and got Duryodhana to invite the Pandavas over to his court for a game of dice (gambling). He was then enticed by Duryodhana and Shakuni to place his brothers as bets.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Yudhishthira fell for the ruse and bet _____, losing her too
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana now played another trick and told Yudhishthira that he still had his wife Draupadi to place as a bet and if Yudhishthira won, he would return everything to the Pandavas. Yudhishthira fell for the ruse and bet Draupadi, losing her too.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: At this point, _____ ordered that Draupadi, who was now a slave to him, be brought to the court
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana now played another trick and told Yudhishthira that he still had his wife Draupadi to place as a bet and if Yudhishthira won, he would return everything to the Pandavas. At this point, Duryodhana ordered that Draupadi, who was now a slave to him, be brought to the court.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Duryodhana then ordered _____ to disrobe Draupadi before everyone, as a slave girl has no rights
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana's younger brother Dushasana dragged Draupadi to the royal court, pulling her by her hair, insulting her dignity and asserting that she, like the Pandava brothers, was now their servant. Duryodhana then ordered Dushasana to disrobe Draupadi before everyone, as a slave girl has no rights.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Dushasana, shocked and tired, gave up on disrobing _____
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana then ordered Dushasana to disrobe Draupadi before everyone, as a slave girl has no rights. Dushasana, shocked and tired, gave up on disrobing Draupadi.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Arjuna performed penance and won the entire gamut of celestial weapons (_____) as boons from the gods
Pandava.fact: Arjuna performed penance and won the entire gamut of celestial weapons (Divyastras) as boons from the gods.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: They spent the 13th year in ajnatavasa masquerading as peasants in the service of the royal family of _____, the king of Matsya
Pandava.fact: They spent the 13th year in ajnatavasa masquerading as peasants in the service of the royal family of Virata, the king of Matsya.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Duryodhana refused to yield _____
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana refused to yield Indraprastha. For the sake of peace and to avert a disastrous war, Krishna proposed that if Hastinapura agrees to give the Pandavas only five villages named Indraprastha (Delhi), Swarnprastha (Sonipat), Panprastha (Panipat), Vyaghrprastha (Baghpat) and Tilprastha (Tilpat) if these five villages given they would be satisfied and would make no more demands.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Thus the stage was set for the great war, for which the epic of _____ is known most of all
Pandava.fact: Thus the stage was set for the great war, for which the epic of Mahabharata is known most of all.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Duryodhana reached first and _____ was just behind him
Pandava.fact: When the Kurukshetra war was going to be held, both Arjuna on behalf of the Pandavas, and Duryodhana on behalf of the Kauravas, went to Krishna to seek help. Duryodhana reached first and Arjuna was just behind him.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: They entered _____'s room and found him sleeping
Pandava.fact: When the Kurukshetra war was going to be held, both Arjuna on behalf of the Pandavas, and Duryodhana on behalf of the Kauravas, went to Krishna to seek help. They entered Krishna's room and found him sleeping.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Duryodhana sat on a raised chair near _____'s head and Arjuna sat near Krishna's feet closing his hands
Pandava.fact: When the Kurukshetra war was going to be held, both Arjuna on behalf of the Pandavas, and Duryodhana on behalf of the Kauravas, went to Krishna to seek help. They entered Krishna's room and found him sleeping.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: When Krishna woke up, he saw _____ first and asked him about the purpose of his visit
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana reached first and Arjuna was just behind him. Duryodhana sat on a raised chair near Krishna's head and Arjuna sat near Krishna's feet closing his hands.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Then he found _____ sitting next to him, and asked him the same question
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana sat on a raised chair near Krishna's head and Arjuna sat near Krishna's feet closing his hands. Then he found Duryodhana sitting next to him, and asked him the same question.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Krishna was then told that war was going to be held and Arjuna and _____ had come to him seeking his military help
Pandava.fact: Duryodhana sat on a raised chair near Krishna's head and Arjuna sat near Krishna's feet closing his hands. Then he found Duryodhana sitting next to him, and asked him the same question.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: To this _____ replied that he had seen Arjuna first and so he would give him priority, and asked what he needed
Pandava.fact: When Krishna woke up, he saw Arjuna first and asked him about the purpose of his visit. Krishna was then told that war was going to be held and Arjuna and Duryodhana had come to him seeking his military help.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He gave _____ two options – either his army of 100,000 soldiers or Krishna himself who shall not fight in the war
Pandava.fact: Krishna was then told that war was going to be held and Arjuna and Duryodhana had come to him seeking his military help. To this Krishna replied that he had seen Arjuna first and so he would give him priority, and asked what he needed.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: To this _____ immediately opted for Krishna for his help and thus Duryodhana was given Krishna's army
Pandava.fact: Krishna was then told that war was going to be held and Arjuna and Duryodhana had come to him seeking his military help. To this Krishna replied that he had seen Arjuna first and so he would give him priority, and asked what he needed.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: In the end, all 100 _____ brothers and their entire army was slain, with only three surviving on their side
Pandava.fact: In the end, all 100 Kaurava brothers and their entire army was slain, with only three surviving on their side. At the end of the war, only 10 survived the war on both sides, namely Ashvatthama, Kripa, and Kritavarma on the Kaurava side and the five Pandavas, Krishna and Satyaki on the Pandava side.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: After having won the war, _____ was crowned the king
Pandava.fact: After having won the war, Yudhishthira was crowned the king.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Shortly after _____ left the Earth, they all decided that the time had come for them to renounce the world, as the age of Kali Yuga had started
Pandava.fact: At the end of the war, only 10 survived the war on both sides, namely Ashvatthama, Kripa, and Kritavarma on the Kaurava side and the five Pandavas, Krishna and Satyaki on the Pandava side. Shortly after Krishna left the Earth, they all decided that the time had come for them to renounce the world, as the age of Kali Yuga had started.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: For this purpose, they all climbed _____, which leads to Svarga
Pandava.fact: For this purpose, they all climbed Mount Kailash, which leads to Svarga.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: On their way, all except _____ slipped and died one by one
Pandava.fact: On their way, all except Yudhishthira slipped and died one by one. Yudhishthira was accompanied by a dog who was none other than Yama himself.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Yudhishthira was accompanied by a dog who was none other than _____ himself
Pandava.fact: Yudhishthira was accompanied by a dog who was none other than Yama himself.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: The first to die was _____; she was imperfect because she loved Arjuna more than her other husbands
Pandava.fact: The first to die was Draupadi; she was imperfect because she loved Arjuna more than her other husbands.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Then it was _____, imperfect because he was overconfident about his knowledge in science
Pandava.fact: Then it was Sahadeva, imperfect because he was overconfident about his knowledge in science.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He was followed by _____, imperfect because he was over-enthusiastic about his good looks
Pandava.fact: He was followed by Nakula, imperfect because he was over-enthusiastic about his good looks.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Then fell _____, imperfect because he was proud of his skills—he challenged Hanuman and Shiva
Pandava.fact: The first to die was Draupadi; she was imperfect because she loved Arjuna more than her other husbands. Then fell Arjuna, imperfect because he was proud of his skills—he challenged Hanuman and Shiva.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Next was _____, imperfect because he killed his enemies brutally—thus enjoyed their sufferings
Pandava.fact: Next was Bhima, imperfect because he killed his enemies brutally—thus enjoyed their sufferings.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: On reaching heaven, he did not find either his virtuous brothers or his wife _____
Pandava.fact: On reaching heaven, he did not find either his virtuous brothers or his wife Draupadi.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Instead, he finds _____ sitting on a divine throne
Pandava.fact: Instead, he finds Karna sitting on a divine throne.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: He wanted an explanation from _____, the lord of death
Pandava.fact: He wanted an explanation from Yama, the lord of death. Yama explained that the Kauravas had been allowed into heaven because they died as warriors on the battlefield.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Yama explained that the _____ had been allowed into heaven because they died as warriors on the battlefield
Pandava.fact: Yama explained that the Kauravas had been allowed into heaven because they died as warriors on the battlefield.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Once the debt had been repaid, they would join them in _____
Pandava.fact: Once the debt had been repaid, they would join them in Svarga.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Though initially he was tempted to flee, he mastered himself and remained after hearing the voices of his beloved brothers and _____ calling out to him, asking him to stay with them in their misery
Pandava.fact: Though initially he was tempted to flee, he mastered himself and remained after hearing the voices of his beloved brothers and Draupadi calling out to him, asking him to stay with them in their misery.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Yama explained to _____ that it was all illusion created by Yama himself
Pandava.fact: Yudhishthira decided to remain, ordering the divine charioteer to return. Yama explained to Yudhishthira that it was all illusion created by Yama himself.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: It was a punishment to _____ to feel sad and soak tears on seeing his beloved ones being punished
Pandava.fact: Yama explained to Yudhishthira that it was all illusion created by Yama himself. It was a punishment to Yudhishthira to feel sad and soak tears on seeing his beloved ones being punished.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: It was because _____ felt sad on hearing fake news that his son was dead
Pandava.fact: It was because Drona felt sad on hearing fake news that his son was dead. Yudhishthira told the message incompletely due to which Drona felt sad and cried in grief.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Yudhishthira told the message incompletely due to which _____ felt sad and cried in grief
Pandava.fact: It was because Drona felt sad on hearing fake news that his son was dead. Yudhishthira told the message incompletely due to which Drona felt sad and cried in grief.

Pandava.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Pandava.question: Because of this, _____ had to feel sad in a similar manner
Pandava.fact: It was a punishment to Yudhishthira to feel sad and soak tears on seeing his beloved ones being punished. Yudhishthira told the message incompletely due to which Drona felt sad and cried in grief.
